content.goal: Enable a greenhouse monitoring sensing node that measures temperature, humidity, soil moisture, and light, and reports readings remotely while confirming deployment environment, measurement accuracy, sampling/reporting intervals, and power/communication constraints before component selection.
content.problemStatement: The greenhouse sensing node must begin with a functional architecture, but key constraints for deployment environment, acceptable accuracy/error bounds, periodic sampling/reporting cadence, and remote communication/power feasibility are not yet confirmed. The prototype must not assume specific component choices prematurely.
content.intendedContext: An early-stage team will prototype the node and review timestamped measurements and remote summaries to decide next embedded constraints and component steps.
scope: Functional specification for multi-modal environmental sensing and periodic acquisition.
Functional design for timestamped storage, remote reporting, and analysis-ready summaries.
Explicit identification of unknown constraints (accuracy, sampling/reporting cadence, deployment exposure, and power/communication).
outOfScope: Component-part selection (specific sensor modules, MCUs, radios, protocols, and cloud platforms).
Firmware libraries, PCB layout, schematic validation, and simulation execution.
Production manufacturing planning and long-term deployment operations.
successCriteria: All produced artifacts conform to the v1 contracts.
Explicit and inferred requirements are distinguishable.
Unsupported assumptions are not presented as facts.
The Next Action is derived from concrete blockers and open questions about greenhouse monitoring constraints.

assumptions.statement: Initial prototypes can operate with placeholder constraints for accuracy and cadence until the user confirms target values for the remote reporting workflow.
Remote reporting requirements can be represented functionally without committing to a specific communication technology in this phase.
